answer: Group new agents into cohorts by the week they join, and give each cohort one fixed slice of rewards for its first year, shared among its members. Like a sonnet, the slice has a set number of lines however many voices crowd in. Fifty fakes spun up on Monday mostly split the pay their own farm would have earned, and spreading them over months costs patience while each week's slice stays thin. Honest newcomers arrive like grass on a knoll, a few at a time, and each keeps a share worth more than jade.
